scenes.heading: Fraction problem solving
scenes.sub: Half of what is left is not half!
scenes.say: Spend a third, then give away half of what is left. How much do you have now? Today you will learn to solve fraction problems with several steps, and even work backwards to the start.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Your friend eats half a pizza, then you eat half of what is left
scenes.science: Half of the remaining half is 1/2 × 1/2 = 1/4 of the pizza
scenes.breaks: A pizza only cuts into a few slices, but numbers split into any fraction, like 7/13 of $91.
scenes.say: Your friend eats half a pizza. Then you eat half of what is left. You did not eat half a pizza. You ate half of the leftover half, which is one quarter. The words of what is left change what the fraction is a fraction of.
scenes.caption: Your friend eats half a pizza. Then you eat half of what is left. You ate half of the leftover half: 1/2 × 1/2 = 1/4. "Of what is left" changes what the fraction is a fraction of.

scenes.heading: A fraction of WHAT?

left.title: Of the whole
points: Both are of the same whole

scenes.say: Always ask: a fraction of what? If both fractions are of the whole, you can add them. If the second fraction is of what is left, find the remainder first, then multiply the fractions that are left.

scenes.heading: A bar model
scenes.say: Here is one hundred and twenty dollars drawn as a bar of four equal parts. Shoes take one part, thirty dollars. That leaves ninety dollars. Two thirds of the ninety is sixty dollars for the jacket, so thirty dollars is left.
scenes.caption: $120 drawn as a bar of 4 equal parts. Shoes take one part: $30. That leaves $90. 2/3 of $90 is $60 for the jacket, so $30 is left.

scenes.heading: Working backwards
scenes.say: To work backwards, divide the part by its fraction. If three fifths of a number is twenty-four, one fifth is eight, and the whole is forty.
scenes.caption: To work backwards, divide the part by its fraction. If 3/5 of a number is 24, 1/5 is 8, and the whole is 40.

scenes.heading: Back to the start
scenes.question: Ana spends 2/5 of her money, then 1/2 of what is left. She has $18 left. How much did she start with?
scenes.say: Ana spends two fifths, so three fifths is left. Then she keeps half of that: three tenths. Three tenths is eighteen dollars, so one tenth is six dollars, and she started with sixty dollars.
scenes.caption: Ana spends 2/5, so 3/5 is left. She keeps half of that: 3/10. 3/10 is $18, so 1/10 is $6, and she started with $60.

scenes.heading: The same problem as a bar
notes: Use 10 boxes so every fraction fits
scenes.say: In a bar of ten boxes, the first four are spent, the next three are spent, and the last three are the eighteen dollars. Each box is six dollars, so ten boxes make sixty.
scenes.caption: In a bar of 10 boxes, 4 are spent first, 3 are spent next, and the last 3 are the $18. Each box is $6, so 10 boxes make $60.

points: Remainder steps: multiply what is left
scenes.say: Quick recap. Ask what each fraction is a fraction of. For remainder steps, multiply the fractions that are left. Draw a bar model. To work backwards, divide the part by the fraction, then check forwards. Now try the practice questions!
